correctness.rationale: At the synchronous equilibrium, t=s(s−1) and a=(s−1)/s. Linearization differentiates the current numerator and lagged squared denominator to a and −2a. Diagonalizing the spatial shift gives all k quadratics lambda²−a omega lambda+2a omega. For a<1/2 the Schur condition is exactly H(a,Re omega)>0. Its minimizing mode(s) have the smallest cosine; the derivative −6a(3−2a Re omega−8a²) is strictly negative throughout this interval, so the sign change determines the unique first threshold. At equality the product has modulus below one, leaving one unit root and one interior root per critical mode, and all other modes are strictly stable. A critical mode is expanding above the crossing up to 1/2 by the strict Schur violation away from equality. Exactly at a=1/2, if neither root expanded their moduli would both equal one and b−conj(b)c would vanish for the quadratic lambda²+b lambda+c; here it is a(2a−omega), nonzero in a critical mode. For a>1/2 expansion follows from the product. The even-case factorization expands correctly and the sole critical multiplier is −1; real unit multipliers are excluded for odd k. Simplicity and the positive radial derivative establish transversality. Differentiating H at a=1/3, u=−1 gives the claimed odd-k asymptotics after converting a to t. The in-phase mode remains contracting until t=2.
residual_risks: Numerical tests do not prove arbitrary k; the spectral argument does. The threshold specifies neither a nonlinear bifurcation nor global attraction.

value.rationale: A sharp threshold and the identity of the destabilizing modes resolve what a sufficient norm bound and the synchronous scalar analysis leave open. The parity law separates a single alternating negative multiplier from a genuinely nonreal pair; the strict extension of the stable interval for odd rings and its k^(-2) scale quantify this difference.
residual_risks: The value is the exact linear spectral classification, not a nonlinear bifurcation diagnosis.
